body_excerpt:
Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in Kibana Leading to Denial of Service

Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Kibana can lead to a denial of service via Excessive Allocation (CAPEC-130). An authenticated user holding only low, read-level Agent Builder privileges could submit a specially crafted request that causes Kibana to consume an unbounded amount of memory, terminating the process and denying service to all users of the instance.

Affected Versions:

  • 9.x: All versions from 9.3.0 up to and including 9.4.5

Users on the 8.x release line are not affected. The Agent Builder feature that contains this vulnerability was introduced in Kibana 9.3.0 and is not present in the 8.x release line.

Affected Configurations:
Kibana deployments with the Agent Builder feature enabled.

Solutions and Mitigations:

The issue is resolved in Kibana version 9.4.6.

For Users that Cannot Upgrade:

There are no workarounds for this vulnerability.

Indicators of Compromise (IOC)

No specific indicators of compromise have been identified for this vulnerability.

Elastic Cloud Serverless

Due to our continuous deployment and patching model, the vulnerability described in this security advisory was remediated in our Elastic Cloud Serverless offering before the public disclosure.
